items.title: From Nepal’s floods to the world order: Reading Shah’s first UN address
items.desc: Nepal Prime Minister turns a warning from ‘roof of the world’ into a broader argument for climate justice, stronger regional cooperation and a multilateral system more responsive to vulnerable countries.

items.title: Adverse weather disrupts domestic flights as five airports remain closed
items.desc: More than 130 domestic departures are scheduled on Friday, but low visibility leaves passengers waiting.

items.title: Shah meets Albanese, Australia reiterates support for flood-hit Nepal
items.desc: The Australian prime minister expressed solidarity with Nepal and families of missing Australians during the meeting on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.

items.title: Trump welcomes China’s Xi with fanfare, but no breakthroughs emerge
items.desc: Trump and Xi traded warm rhetoric at a high-profile White House summit, but offered few signs of progress on Taiwan, AI, trade and the Iran war.

items.title: Major highways hit by landslides as heavy rain persists
items.desc: Persistent rain has blocked or restricted several major roads, with authorities imposing overnight closures and warning travellers of further landslide risks.

items.title: In New York, Foreign Minister Khanal introduces Nepal’s new political order
items.desc: Shisir Khanal discusses the Gen Z movement, the rise of a new political class and the government’s economic and foreign policy priorities.

items.title: Balendra Shah UN speech: Full transcript of Nepal prime minister’s address to the 81st UN General Assembly
items.desc: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s full UN speech on the Bhotekoshi floods, climate justice, Himalayan cooperation, climate finance and reform of the global order.

items.title: Five takeaways from Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s UN address
items.desc: The prime minister linked Nepal’s floods to climate risks, proposed cooperation in the Himalayas, and called for fairer climate finance and a more equitable global order.

items.title: Nobody knows how to count a smile like that
items.desc: A glacier fell in Nepal. In the two weeks that followed, I watched three separate systems fail the same woman.

items.title: Nepal women lock up kabaddi bronze, target bigger prize
items.desc: A 34-25 victory over Sri Lanka sends the women’s team into the Asian Games semifinals. Up next is a showdown against world powerhouse India.

items.title: Nepal seek redemption against Afghanistan 12 years after Incheon heartbreak
items.desc: Nepal had lost to Afghanistan in the quarterfinals of the 2014 Asian Games in South Korea. Now, the duo come face to face after over a decade.

items.title: Pokhara International Airport welcomed its first daily international flight. Can the government sustain it?
items.desc: The flight should not lead to complacency among Nepal’s authorities.

items.title: Why Modi needs to embrace a little political banter
items.desc: Everything is fair game for the BJP, including viciously mocking leaders of the opposition, but the prime minister must be treated with only the highest level of respect.

items.title: In Achham, fewer children means fewer classrooms
items.desc: Declining births, out-migration and a shift towards smaller families are leaving early childhood centres short of pupils and forcing some schools to close.

items.title: Flood-hit women entrepreneurs determined to rebuild their businesses
items.desc: With family members dead or missing, many women see the need to rise up and find work to support their children and remaining ones.

items.title: Dhunibesi taxes scrap despite constitutional ban
items.desc: The municipality in Dhading collects Rs3.39 per kg from scrap trucks leaving the Valley, although the constitution bars local governments from taxing goods moving from one jurisdiction to another.

items.title: Bidya Bhandari’s return may give UML’s power struggle a new twist
items.desc: UML’s electoral drubbing has brought her back at a moment when the UML chief is under pressure to rethink his leadership.

items.title: From flood disaster to climate warning, Shah makes the Himalayas his UN message
items.desc: Nepal’s prime minister calls for a Himalayan climate-resilience mechanism, more grant-based finance, and stronger regional early-warning systems as climate extremes threaten mountain communities.

items.title: Shah raises climate risks and Bhotekoshi disaster with Guterres
items.desc: PM seeks UN support for riverbank resettlement, green reconstruction and an extension of Nepal’s LDC graduation timeline.

items.title: At the UN, Shah to bring Nepal’s climate crisis into focus
items.desc: The world’s youngest national leader makes his UN debut as Nepal seeks greater support for communities bearing the costs of climate disasters.

items.title: Congress to elect thousands of young faces to its ranks
items.desc: At least 13,483 people under 35 are guaranteed places in party committees from the ward to the central level, with more young members winning leadership posts through open competition.

items.title: Friendly rivalry turns fiery as Bista and Chaudhary headline debut Fusion Fight
items.desc: Tied 1-1 in career head-to-heads, Nepal’s top female Muay Thai fighters trade knockout threats ahead of their October 10 face-off.
